title: Web: shell, BFF, lib and configuration
summary: The web shell, BFF and lib are small and deliberately bounded. Every proxied operation passes one pure Host, Origin, Sec-Fetch-Site and double-submit guard, then a session check, before forward() adds the internal token and the cookie-chosen workspace. The API checks membership again (Decision 0023 E3). Server modules carry server-only, the proxy route handlers are one-liners, the exact Luma tokens are imported unedited, and every input, select and textarea goes through components/ui. The weak points are failure handling and how deeply responses are validated. The hand-written api-client validator ignores minItems, maxItems and schema-valued additionalProperties, which leaves 29 constraints in 19 generated schemas unchecked. requestJson reports HTTP failures as ContractError. Every catch in service-status.ts and bff.ts throws away its cause without logging it, so contract drift, a 401, a timeout and a missing environment variable all end up as 'Sign in', a generic 503 or a bare 500. Sign-in reports an outage as a wrong password. Each component writes its own mutation code: 20 response bodies are type-asserted and the generated parseErrorResponse is never used. They all sit on a csrfFetch that rotates the token on every write, so two overlapping writes can refuse each other. The tooling enforces less than it seems to. schema-value.test.ts never runs because verify.py names unit tests one by one. ESLint has no type-aware, assertion or size rules. packages/api-client is outside lint and format. DH-06's Vitest and React Testing Library layer is missing: US-1.3 deferred it, and no decision records node:test as its substitute. Size is not the problem in this area. I read the code behind the metric leads for guardRequest's complexity, the primitive files with several components and the test-fixture type assertion, and judged all three acceptable.

scores.why: Strict flags (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes), pinned versions and separate lint, typegen and typecheck steps meet DH-06 as written. ESLint has no assertion, size or type-aware rules, api-client is outside lint and format, and the Vitest/RTL layer is missing without a decision.
Server-only modules, a pure guard and one forwarder make the boundaries clear. Alias routes, a credential module the app never calls and an incomplete primitive set blur the public surface.
The largest file is 175 lines. Four components run 63 to 75 lines, and forward() and guardRequest reach complexity 13. All modest.
Most functions do one thing. forward() and AccountFooter each mix policy or derived state with output.
The layout follows Next.js conventions and the DH-03 placement of apps/web and packages/api-client. Three alias routes give some endpoints two URLs.

Server Components are the default, reads happen on the server and the SSE pass-through never owns a run. Rotating the CSRF token on every write causes a race, each component writes its own mutation code, and per-render reads are not memoized.
Comments explain why and cite decisions and PRD IDs. Two no longer match the code, and a third gives a focus-order reason that has since changed.
Generated types are used at the server boundary. The runtime validator ignores 29 declared constraints, and 20 client sites type-assert response shapes instead of parsing them.
Every server-side catch throws away its cause without a log. Drift and a 401 both read as signed out, and sign-in reports outages as bad credentials.

The guard and credential tests are table-driven on shared fixtures, and boundary.spec.ts covers the BFF end to end. One unit test never runs, body limits are untested, and there is no fast layer for BFF or client logic.
Readable, well-bounded code. Its main costs are failures nobody can see, a validator weaker than its contract, and mutation code repeated across screens.

strengths.title: A pure, table-tested request guard
strengths.evidence: apps/web/lib/request-guard.ts:33-67 has no framework dependency and compares tokens in constant time (22-31). apps/web/tests/unit/request-guard.test.ts:31-76 tests it against forged hosts, DNS rebinding through localhost, cross-site and same-site fetches, and missing, empty and mismatched tokens.

strengths.title: Server-only boundaries held in code, not convention
strengths.evidence: import "server-only" is line 1 of apps/web/lib/bff.ts, session.ts, server-config.ts, service-status.ts and workspace-choice.ts. Configuration is read on each call (server-config.ts:11). The internal token goes onto a fresh Headers object, so a client-sent Authorization or X-Autobots-Internal never gets through (bff.ts:59-62, 80-89). The Supabase client stays on the server behind an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie (session.ts:10-21), and accessToken says outright that nothing trusts the token's contents (session.ts:37).

strengths.title: One path for every proxied operation
strengths.evidence: Every proxy route calls forward() or streamFrom(). Their authorized() runs the guard, then the session check, then attaches the chosen workspace (apps/web/lib/bff.ts:37-69). The stream route validates its cursor and encodes the run id (apps/web/app/api/v1/runs/[id]/events/stream/route.ts:12-17). Only the stream's reader is tied to the browser, so a disconnect never cancels a run (bff.ts:128-131).

strengths.title: Exact tokens, consumed rather than copied
strengths.evidence: apps/web/app/globals.css:2-5 imports docs/design/luma.css unedited plus the one documented extension. Lines 31-77 map every color, including the chart and sidebar tokens, and the radius scale to Tailwind (DS-01, DS-03). Dark is the server fallback, and hydration suppression is limited to the root element (apps/web/app/layout.tsx:19-23). Invalid saved themes are removed before paint (layout.tsx:13-17).

strengths.title: Form controls fully centralized
strengths.evidence: apps/web/components/ui/field.tsx provides Input, Textarea, Select and Choice with data-slot markers, and keeps Decision 0023 E1's border in one constant (field.tsx:10-11). git grep finds no raw <input>, <select> or <textarea> in app/ or components/ outside components/ui.

strengths.title: State never carried by color alone
strengths.evidence: SidebarNav marks the current page with aria-current, fill and weight (apps/web/components/sidebar-nav.tsx:69, 95-99) and gives the pending count screen-reader words (120). Badge and readiness put the meaning in words (badge.tsx:6, readiness.tsx:15). ServiceStatusBadge keeps "Python API: available" whole for assistive technology (service-status-badge.tsx:6-7). The shell opens with a skip link (app-shell.tsx:25-30).

strengths.title: Cross-language fixtures instead of parallel test data
strengths.evidence: apps/web/tests/unit/credential-precedence.test.ts:9-23 and packages/api-client/tests/contract.test.ts:8-20 read the same contracts/fixtures files as the Python tests (services/agent/tests/test_contracts.py:30). contract.test.ts:22-25 pins that a cast cannot stand in for validation.

strengths.title: Promise handling already clean
strengths.evidence: Event handlers mark fire-and-forget calls with void (apps/web/components/account-form.tsx:49, workspace-chooser.tsx:48). A read-only ESLint run on this area with type-aware no-floating-promises and no-misused-promises found no violation in production code, so those rules can be enforced at no cost.

findings.title: The contract validator ignores array bounds, map value schemas and unknown keywords

locations.note: The array branch checks items only. minItems and maxItems are never read.
Extra properties are checked only when additionalProperties is false. A schema value is skipped.
The index signature admits any keyword, and the switch default (137-138) accepts an unknown type.
ModelPolicyState.role_overrides values must be a ModelProfileId. This is never checked.
WorkflowGraph.nodes has maxItems 200. This is never checked.
A consumer that trusts the parsed role overrides
The shared fixtures cover four models and no array bound or map value.

findings.impact: Generated parse functions are the only runtime check at the TypeScript trust boundary. Even so, parseModelPolicyState accepts a role override that names an unapproved profile, parseJobsChart accepts an empty or 26-hour chart, and parseWorkflowGraph accepts 201 nodes. The TypeScript side validates less than Pydantic. If Pydantic starts emitting a keyword this runtime ignores (oneOf with a discriminator for a tagged union, for example), every value would pass silently. That is the drift the shared fixtures exist to catch.
findings.recommendation: Write the failing cases first. In contracts/fixtures/boundary-cases.json, which both languages read, add a WorkflowGraph with 201 nodes and a ModelPolicyState whose role_overrides names an unapproved profile, and add ModelPolicyState to both model maps. Then implement minItems, maxItems and schema-valued additionalProperties in runtime.ts. Add a contract test that walks every schema position in `schemas` and fails on any keyword the runtime does not implement. Allow annotations (title, description, default, examples) explicitly. Leave generated.ts to the generator.
findings.ruleCheck: contracts.md: shared validation fixtures cover both languages, and TypeScript types do not validate JSON. The fix lives in the hand-written runtime.ts, its test and the shared fixtures. generated.ts is regenerated, never edited.
findings.verifierNote: Re-walked `schemas` in generated.ts: 15 maxItems, 4 minItems and 10 schema-valued additionalProperties, 29 constraints in 19 of 170 schemas, and no other unimplemented keyword today. The shared cases cover four models and none of these constraints.

findings.title: Server reads and the BFF throw away every failure cause, so drift, 401s and timeouts read as signed out or a generic 503

locations.note: fetchSession turns any error, including ContractError, into null.
Readiness and pending approvals use the same catch-all null.
forward() turns every failure into 503 service_unavailable without logging it.
streamFrom() does the same.
A null session, whatever caused it, is answered with 401 not_signed_in.
A null session renders the Sign in link.

findings.impact: Several unrelated failures all show a signed-in person the Sign in link: a role value this build does not know, an API on another revision, a missing AUTOBOTS_INTERNAL_TOKEN (the API answers 401), or a 3-second timeout. /api/workspace then tells them "Sign in first." The BFF reports its own 30-second timeout as "The local API is unavailable." No private log records which of these happened, so at runtime nobody can see the contract drift this layer is meant to expose. DH-06 asks for the opposite.
findings.recommendation: Add a server-only logFailure(operation, error). It records the operation, the error class, the ContractError path, the HTTP status and whether a timeout fired. It never records bodies, headers, tokens or query strings, which keeps the promise in bff.ts:33-35. Have service-status return a discriminated result: signed_out only when there is no token or the API answers 401, and unavailable (logged) for everything else. Render Sign in only for signed_out. Answer /api/workspace with 503 when the session read is unavailable. In forward(), log the cause and map a timeout to 504 upstream_timeout. This needs requestJson to keep the HTTP status; see the requestJson finding.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: centralize error handling, preserve causes in private logs and expose safe typed errors. nextjs.md: server keys never reach props or public responses. The log therefore carries only names, codes, statuses and paths, and the browser still sees only the safe envelope.
findings.verifierNote: No console or logger call exists in apps/web app, components or lib, and every cited catch discards its error; security.py:42-45 refuses an empty internal token with 401. WSHL-20 covers the configuration side of the same symptom.

findings.title: requestJson reports HTTP failures as ContractError and drops the API's typed error

locations.note: The status survives only inside the message, and the ErrorResponse body is never read.
ClientOptions.fetch is typed as the full typeof fetch.
The `as typeof fetch` cast that type forces
This test locks in the conflation.

findings.impact: Callers cannot tell 401, 403, 503 and contract drift apart without parsing a message string, which is why service-status treats them all alike. Consumers also have to cast their fetch wrapper, because the option type is wider than requestJson needs.
findings.recommendation: For non-2xx responses, throw an ApiError that carries the status and the parsed JSON body, and keep ContractError for schema violations. Callers read the safe code with the generated parseErrorResponse(error.body). Narrow ClientOptions.fetch to `(url: string, init: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>`, which is all requestJson calls, and remove the cast in service-status.ts. Change contract.test.ts:33-36 first so it expects ApiError.
findings.ruleCheck: contracts.md: Pydantic/OpenAPI owns ErrorResponse, so callers parse it with the generated parser instead of a hand-written shape. runtime.ts is hand-written and generated.ts is untouched. The package keeps erasableSyntaxOnly, so the sketch declares fields rather than using parameter properties.
findings.verifierNote: requestJson throws ContractError for any non-2xx (runtime.ts:168-170), contract.test.ts:33-36 pins it, and service-status.ts holds the only four web calls to generated request functions.

findings.title: csrfFetch mints a new double-submit token for every write, so overlapping writes can refuse each other

locations.note: Every GET mints a token and replaces the cookie.
The header must equal whichever cookie the browser sends at that moment.

findings.impact: Write A fetches token T1, and the cookie becomes T1. Before A is sent, write B (from another tab or a quick second action) fetches T2, and the cookie becomes T2. A then carries header T1 with cookie T2 and is refused with invalid_csrf. Callers show this as a generic failure, and sign-in shows it as a wrong password. Every write also costs an extra round trip. The token reply is type-asserted rather than checked. Spreading init.headers would drop every header if a caller passed a Headers instance or a tuple array, both of which RequestInit allows; no caller does today.
findings.recommendation: Keep one token per browser session. /api/csrf returns the request's existing autobots.csrf value and mints a new one only when there is none, and csrfFetch caches the token in module scope. After an invalid_csrf or missing_csrf refusal, fetch a token once more and resend. The guard refuses before forwarding, so the retry cannot duplicate a write. Check reply.ok and the reply's shape, and build headers with new Headers(init.headers) before setting the token. Add a browser test with two overlapping writes.
findings.ruleCheck: nextjs.md: protect mutations with Host, Origin and CSRF checks. The double-submit comparison, the Origin, Host and Sec-Fetch-Site checks and the SameSite=Strict cookie stay as they are. Only the token's lifetime changes, and double-submit protection does not depend on it.
findings.verifierNote: Every GET /api/csrf mints and sets a new cookie, and 29 csrfFetch calls in 19 files rely on it; the race is reasoned from the code, not observed. The header-spreading problem is marked latent: no caller passes a Headers instance or tuple array.

findings.title: Three route files rebuild the same guard input, error envelope, cookie policy and JSON body read

locations.note: A 403 without Cache-Control: no-store
refused() copies safeError().
Body read with a type assertion
Body read with a type assertion
Session cookie with secure: false
CSRF cookie with secure: false
The workspace cookie derives secure from the origin.

findings.impact: A new route that does not go through the proxy has to copy the guard by hand, and the existing copies have already diverged. On an https origin only the workspace cookie would be Secure, and one refusal response lacks no-store.
findings.recommendation: Move this shared preamble into one server-only module. refusalFor(request) builds GuardInput once and returns the 403 response or null. jsonError(status, code, message) always sets no-store. readJsonObject(request) returns a record or null, which removes both assertions. cookieOptions(config, httpOnly) serves the session, CSRF and workspace cookies. Type the refusal codes as a GuardRefusal union in request-guard.ts. Keep every check and its order; request-guard.test.ts and boundary.spec.ts already cover them.
findings.ruleCheck: nextjs.md: verify session and workspace on every BFF operation, and protect mutations with Host, Origin and CSRF checks. The extraction keeps each check in the same order. Decision 0023 E3's HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict workspace cookie keeps its flags.
findings.verifierNote: The three GuardInput literals, the missing no-store at session/route.ts:27-30, both body assertions and the three secure settings confirmed. XDUP-12 reports the same duplication from the lens.

findings.title: Each component writes its own mutation code: 20 type-asserted response bodies and no shared helper

locations.note: The only shared piece, and it returns a raw Response.
A local mutate() helper
Another local mutate() helper
A local send() helper (run-panel.tsx:84 has another)
Asserted error body

findings.impact: DH-06 asks for explicit response parsing and no blanket assertions. Yet 20 places read error codes from unchecked shapes, and every form repeats the same busy, try, catch and message sequence. That sequence is most of why AccountForm (63 lines) and SignInForm (66 lines) exceed the 60-line metric lead.
findings.recommendation: Add a browser-side sendJson(path, { method, body, parse, idempotencyKey }) built on csrfFetch. On success it returns the value parsed by the generated parser. On failure it returns the status and the error parsed by parseErrorResponse, or null when that body fails its contract or the network fails. Migrate this area's three forms first, and the other screens when they are next touched.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: use generated API types, parse responses explicitly at untrusted boundaries, avoid blanket type assertions, and rely on server idempotency for duplicate submits (the helper carries Idempotency-Key). contracts.md: ErrorResponse comes from the generated client.
findings.verifierNote: Recounted: 20 casts of this form in 15 files (19 on failure bodies; continue-run.tsx:53 casts a success body), 29 csrfFetch calls in 19 files and 28 JSON Content-Type literals in 18 files. WSYS-02 should use this same helper.

findings.title: Sign-in reports an unavailable service as a wrong password, and sign-out fails silently
findings.impact: When Supabase Auth or the network is down, people are told their credentials are wrong and may retry or reset a password for nothing. A refused sign-out leaves them signed in with no message. DH-06 asks for unavailable and retryable states to be shown deliberately.
findings.recommendation: In the route, keep 401 sign_in_failed for credential errors, still without saying which field failed. Answer Auth transport errors and 5xx statuses with 503 service_unavailable in the BFF's envelope. In the form, show the credential message only for 401, an unavailable message for 503 or a network failure, and a prompt to reload for a 403 refusal. Show a message when sign-out fails.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: represent loading, empty, denied, unavailable and retryable states deliberately. The 401 message still does not reveal whether the email exists.
findings.verifierNote: The route maps every Auth error to 401 sign_in_failed (51-55), the form shows the credential sentence for any non-ok reply or rejection, and SignOutButton ignores its reply.

findings.title: schema-value.test.ts never runs, because verify.py names unit tests one by one

locations.note: No test script
Only src/ is type-checked, not tests/.
Says fast passed web unit tests after this test was added

findings.evidence:
```py
Step('web_unit_tests', (str(Path(tools.node_dir) / 'node'), '--test', 'apps/web/tests/unit/request-guard.test.ts',
                       'apps/web/tests/unit/credential-precedence.test.ts'), root),
```
.checks/full/latest.json records exactly that argv and 33 tests (14 plus 19), none of them from schema-value.test.ts. The US-16.2 record cites this test as the evidence for a passing scenario.
findings.impact: Any web unit test added beyond these two passes when run by hand but is skipped by every profile. The US-16.2 evidence reads as if the profile ran it, and contributors have no package script that runs the folder.
findings.recommendation: Add a test:unit script to apps/web/package.json that runs node --test over tests/unit/**/*.test.ts, and have the verify step call that script so new files are picked up. Propose the verify.py change to the scripts owners. Put packages/api-client/tests under a type-checked tsconfig, for example a tsconfig.test.json that api_client_typecheck includes.
findings.ruleCheck: AGENTS.md: skipped tests never count as passing implementation evidence. verify.py belongs to the scripts area, so this review only proposes the change.
findings.verifierNote: verify.py:161-162 names two files; .checks/full/latest.json records that argv and 33 passing tests, none from schema-value.test.ts, while the US-16.2 record says fast passed web unit tests.

findings.title: Lint and format enforce only the Next.js presets, and packages/api-client is outside both

locations.note: lint and format:check cover apps/web only.
125 characters. 15 lines here exceed Prettier's 80.
erasableSyntaxOnly is set here but not in apps/web/tsconfig.json, although web unit tests also run under Node type stripping.

findings.evidence:
```js
const config = [
  { ignores: [".next/**", "next-env.d.ts"] },
  ...nextCoreWebVitals,
  ...nextTypescript,
];
```
The measurement found 94 type assertions, 83 functions over 60 lines and 31 functions over complexity 10, and no rule holds any of these at their current level. I ran ESLint read-only on this area with projectService plus no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises, switch-exhaustiveness-check and no-unnecessary-type-assertion. It found no violation in production code, only node:test calls.
findings.impact: DH-06's rules against blanket assertions and for small functions depend on review alone, and the hand-written contract validator has no lint or format gate at all. Lint runs with --max-warnings=0, so any rule added at warn level fails the check immediately, which means there is no way to ratchet today.
findings.recommendation: Add the type-aware promise and exhaustiveness rules as errors now, since they have no production hits, and turn no-floating-promises off for tests/unit. Report size, complexity and assertion rules from a separate non-blocking ESLint run, as the measurement step did. Then record per-file baselines as overrides, then make the rules errors. Extend lint and format:check to packages/api-client, and add erasableSyntaxOnly to apps/web/tsconfig.json.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: pinned ESLint with Next.js, React and TypeScript rules, Prettier, and lint run explicitly. nextjs.md: lint separately from Next.js 16 builds. Nothing here touches next build.
findings.verifierNote: Re-ran the four type-aware rules read-only on all of apps/web: no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises and switch-exhaustiveness-check have no production hit (7 hits in tests/unit), while no-unnecessary-type-assertion has 3 at home-activity.tsx:79-81 and needs a baseline.

findings.title: DH-06's Vitest and Testing Library layer is missing without a recorded decision, and BFF policy has no fast test

locations.note: Playwright and axe only
Body limits. No test asserts 413 or request_too_large.
currentWorkspace has no unit test.
No test
Relative .ts import, because node:test cannot resolve @/ aliases or server-only
US-1.3 deferred Vitest and Testing Library to the first story with behavior to test

findings.evidence: DH-06: "Use Vitest/React Testing Library for relevant pure/client behavior". apps/web has three node:test files covering 3 of its 13 lib modules, and no component tests. git grep for 413, request_too_large and "too large" under apps/web/tests finds nothing. The US-1.3 proposal deferred Vitest and Testing Library to the story that first had behavior to test, and no decision under docs/engineering/decisions mentions Vitest or node:test since. boundary.spec.ts covers the Host, CSRF, internal-token and unavailable cases, but runs only in the db and full profiles.
findings.impact: The fast profile cannot exercise BFF policy, csrfFetch, workspace selection or any client component, so each such change waits for the browser suites. The run body limit from PRD-Tool-Catalog FI-01 is not tested at any level.
findings.recommendation: Choose one of two paths. Either record a decision that node:test replaces Vitest for pure modules, or adopt Vitest and Testing Library with path-alias resolution under an authorized story, since that is a dependency install. Either way, keep fast-testable logic in modules with no server-only or '@/' imports, as request-guard.ts is: plain Node cannot resolve server-only from apps/web, whatever condition is passed. Then extract bff.ts's pure policy and test the body limits, header allowlists and relay first.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06 names Vitest and React Testing Library, so a deviation needs a recorded decision. AGENTS.md: install dependencies only when a story requires them, pinned and recorded.
findings.verifierNote: Line 141, the missing 413 test and the absent decision confirmed, and the US-1.3 deferral added. Revised: server-only is not resolvable by plain Node from apps/web (Next resolves it internally), so --conditions=react-server cannot load those modules.

findings.title: Font sizes and some radii are pixel literals, not tokens

locations.note: @theme maps colors, fonts and radii, but no type scale.
Restates PageHeader's title size
rounded-[10px], which equals rounded-lg
rounded-[10px]

findings.evidence: git grep counts 212 text-[Npx] classes in 39 files across app/ and components/, in 13 distinct sizes: 75 at 12.5px, 63 at 13px and 19 at 13.5px, among others. It also counts rounded-[10px] four times and rounded-[7px] once. The primitives add their own literals: PageHeader's title is text-[32px] and its description text-[14.5px], and Button's sm size is text-[13px]. The sign-in page restates the title size without using PageHeader.
findings.impact: DS-03 asks for consistent typography and a radius scale mapped to the canonical base, and rounded-[10px] just restates --radius. Restyling text means editing 39 files, and new screens keep inventing sizes.
findings.recommendation: Add role-named --text-* tokens to the @theme block (title, lead, row, meta, badge and so on), collapsing the 13 sizes, and never reuse a --color-* name: text-control already means the control border color. Use them in components/ui first, then replace literals as files are touched, and replace rounded-[10px] with rounded-lg. Add a grep ratchet that fails on any new text-[Npx] or rounded-[Npx] class.
findings.ruleCheck: DS-03: map the radius scale to the canonical base and keep typography consistent. DS-01: the color tokens and --radius stay untouched; the new names are a type scale, not a palette change.
findings.verifierNote: Counts reproduced (212 text-[Npx] in 39 files, 13 sizes; rounded-[10px] 4, rounded-[7px] 1), and Button's size moved to line 22. Sketch revised: a Tailwind 4.3.4 compile resolved text-control to --color-control's color and dropped the size, so no size token may reuse a --color-* name.

findings.title: Missing server configuration becomes empty strings and fails far from its cause

locations.note: createServerClient throws on an empty key.
accessToken() runs outside forward()'s try.
new URL() throws on a malformed origin.
new URL() again
The API refuses an empty internal token (fails closed).

findings.evidence:
```ts
internalToken: process.env.AUTOBOTS_INTERNAL_TOKEN ?? "",
...
supabaseAnonKey: process.env.AUTOBOTS_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY ?? "",
```
With the anon key unset, @supabase/ssr's createServerClient throws "Your project's URL and Key are required" (node_modules/@supabase/ssr/dist/main/createServerClient.js:12-13). Because accessToken() runs before forward()'s try (bff.ts:55, 76), every BFF route and the session route answer a bare 500, and service-status turns the same error into signed out. With the internal token unset, the API refuses every call, and the shell again shows Sign in. A malformed AUTOBOTS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN makes new URL() throw in guardRequest and in the workspace route.
findings.impact: A misconfigured local start looks like a signed-out session or a wrong password, and no log names the missing variable. Failing closed is the right outcome; what is missing is a way to tell why.
findings.recommendation: Validate in serverConfig(): require both secrets to be non-empty and the origin to parse as an http(s) origin, and throw a ConfigurationError that names the missing variables but never their values. Catch it in forward(), streamFrom() and the session and workspace routes as 503 server_misconfigured with one log line, and have service-status report unavailable rather than signed out. Keep reading the environment on each call, so nothing is compiled into a build.
